name: BMW K75 / K100
engine: 740 cc triple (K75) or 987 cc four (K100), liquid-cooled, fuel injected, shaft drive
intro: BMW's flying brick. The in-tank fuel pump, the oil/water pump and the splines are the usual jobs.

add.title: Renew the in-tank fuel parts
add.instructions: Pull the fuel pump, its rubber mounts, the hoses and the float. Replace anything that has gone hard or soft. Use hose rated for submerged EFI use.
add.reason: Old fuel kills the pump rubbers and hoses. These are the classic K-bike failures after storage.

add.title: Lube the drive splines
add.instructions: Pull the rear drive and clean and grease the shaft splines with a moly paste. Look for oil in the swingarm.
add.reason: Dry splines wear and fail. Most owners forget to grease them.

F: If the fuel pump won't run, check the side stand switch first. It is in the pump relay circuit.

recallNote: Any recalls on bikes this old were closed long ago.

known.title: Trouble spots
known.what: After the fuel system, the rear crank O-ring and the oil/water pump are the historic trouble spots. They need renewing every decade or two.
